Systematically find multiple coin combinations for a given total
Explain why different coin sets give the same total
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} needs to make exactly 30p, can they find two or three different ways to do it using different combinations of coins?

nodes.description: Recognise Australian coins (5c, 10c, 20c, 50c, $1, $2) and notes ($5, $10, $20, $50, $100), know that a coin's size does not show its value, and solve simple purchase problems within $20 or 20 cents using real coins and virtual money (on-screen coins and notes)
evidence: Sort a mixed handful of real Australian coins into cents coins and dollar coins and explain why the small $2 coin is worth more than the larger 50c coin
Pay exactly for a $7 toy in a money app by dragging a virtual $5 note and a virtual $2 coin
Find the total cost of a $5 book and a $3 pen and say whether a $10 note is enough
nodes.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} plays shop, can they name the Australian coins and notes — like the $1, $2 and 50c coins and the $5 note — and work out if they have enough to buy two things?

nodes.description: Choose and use appropriate standard units to measure length (m/cm), mass (kg/g), temperature (°C), and capacity (litres/ml) to the nearest appropriate unit
evidence: Measure the length of a table in centimetres using a ruler
Weigh an object in grams using a scale
Measure the capacity of a container in millilitres using a measuring jug
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If you ask {{name}} whether to measure a swimming pool or a piece of paper in cm or m, can they pick the sensible unit for each — and explain why?

nodes.description: Compare and order lengths, mass, and capacity and record results using >, <, and =
evidence: Measure two objects and write 45cm > 32cm
Order three containers by capacity after measuring each
Use = when two measurements are the same
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} measures three pieces of string as 15 cm, 9 cm, and 22 cm, can they put them in order from shortest to longest — and write that using a < symbol?

nodes.description: Compare and order the mass and capacity of objects indirectly, using a balance or a third object or container as a go-between, and explain the reasoning
evidence: Use a balance to show the apple is heavier than a block and the block is heavier than the egg, so the apple is heavier than the egg
Pour water from two bottles into the same jug to find which bottle holds more
Order three containers by capacity using cups of rice and explain the order
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wants to know which of two bottles holds more water, can they work it out by pouring each into the same jug and comparing?

nodes.displayName: 比较与排列物体的长度
nodes.description: Order three objects by length and compare the lengths of two objects indirectly using a third object
evidence: Put three ribbons in order from shortest to longest
Use a piece of string to compare the heights of two objects that cannot be placed side by side
Explain that if A is longer than B and B is longer than C, then A is longer than C
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} has three pencils of different lengths but can only compare two at a time, can they figure out which is longest — by using a third pencil as a go-between?

nodes.displayName: 测量长度 · 用相同单位首尾相接
nodes.description: Measure the length of an object using same-size length units laid end to end with no gaps or overlaps
evidence: Measure a book by laying paper clips end to end and counting them
Understand that the length measurement is the number of units that span the object
Avoid gaps and overlaps when placing units
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is measuring the length of a table using identical toy bricks, can they lay them end to end with no gaps — and tell you how many bricks long the table is?

nodes.description: Solve simple money problems involving addition and subtraction, including giving change
evidence: Calculate the total cost of two items priced in pence
Work out change from 50p after buying an item costing 35p
Solve 'How much more money do I need?' problems
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} buys a snack for 45p and pays with a £1 coin, can they work out how much change they should get — and count it back?

nodes.sourceName: Number of minutes in an hour
nodes.displayName: 小时、分钟与一天的关系
nodes.description: Know the number of minutes in an hour and the number of hours in a day
evidence: State that there are 60 minutes in an hour
State that there are 24 hours in a day
Use these facts to solve simple time problems
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} knows there are 60 minutes in an hour, can they tell you how many minutes are in 2 hours — and how many hours make a whole day?

nodes.description: Recognise and use symbols for pounds (£) and pence (p) and combine amounts to make a particular value
evidence: Write £1.50 or 150p correctly
Combine coins to make a given total, e.g. 50p + 20p + 5p = 75p
Read prices written with £ and p symbols
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} picks up coins worth 50p, 20p, and 10p, can they write the total using the p symbol — and tell you if that's enough to buy something costing 75p?

nodes.description: Compare and sequence intervals of time
evidence: Order three events by how long they took
Compare the duration of two activities (e.g. 'the race took longer than the walk')
Sequence intervals on a timeline
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} knows a film takes 2 hours and a car journey takes 45 minutes, can they tell you which takes longer — and put a few daily activities in order of how long they take?

nodes.description: Tell and write the time to five minutes on analogue clocks, including quarter past and quarter to the hour, write these times in digital form, and draw clock hands to show them
evidence: Read an analogue clock showing 3:25 and write the time in digital form as 3:25
Write 'quarter past 9' as 9:15 and 'twenty to four' as 3:40
Draw clock hands to show twenty to four, with the minute hand on 8 and the hour hand just before 4
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If the clock shows quarter to four, can {{name}} tell you the time — and draw hands on a blank clock face to show twenty past three?

nodes.displayName: 加减法应用题 · 长度情境
nodes.description: Solve word problems involving lengths within 100, using addition and subtraction with drawings and equations
evidence: Solve 'The rope is 45 cm long. I cut off 18 cm. How long is it now?'
Draw a diagram (e.g. a ruler drawing) to represent a length word problem
Write an equation with a symbol for the unknown to represent the problem
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} has a piece of rope 75 cm long and cuts off 28 cm, can they work out how much rope is left — and draw a number-line diagram to show it?

nodes.description: Tell and write times to five minutes on analogue and digital clocks with a.m. or p.m. (before or after midday), relating times to daily events and using the words morning, afternoon, evening, noon and midnight. Roman-numeral clock faces and the 24-hour clock are covered in Roman numeral and 24-hour clocks
evidence: Say whether school starts at 8:45 a.m. or 8:45 p.m., and whether bedtime is 7:30 a.m. or 7:30 p.m.
Write 'twenty-five past four in the afternoon' as 4:25 p.m.
Explain that 12 noon is midday, so times just after it are p.m., while times just after midnight are a.m.
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If a clock shows 7:45, can {{name}} tell you the time in words — and say whether breakfast would be at 7:45 a.m. or 7:45 p.m.?

nodes.description: Measure, compare, add, and subtract lengths (m/cm/mm), mass (kg/g), and volume/capacity (l/ml) using standard units
evidence: Measure a length in centimetres and millimetres
Weigh an object using grams and kilograms
Add two measurements in the same unit (e.g. 250 ml + 400 ml = 650 ml)
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} pours 350 ml into a jug and then adds another 275 ml, can they work out the total — and tell you how much more is needed to reach 1 litre?

nodes.description: Measure to determine how much longer one object is than another, expressing the length difference in terms of a standard length unit
evidence: Measure two objects and calculate the difference in length
Express the difference using the correct unit (e.g. '7 cm longer')
Solve a comparison problem: 'How much taller is the bookshelf than the desk?'
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If a pencil is 16 cm and a crayon is 9 cm, can {{name}} work out how much longer the pencil is — without measuring them side by side?

nodes.description: Compare durations of events and calculate the time taken by particular events or tasks
evidence: Work out that a TV show from 5:17 p.m. to 5:43 p.m. lasted 26 minutes
Compare a 35-minute bus journey with a 40-minute walk and say which takes longer and by how much
Solve 'The lesson starts at 10:15 and ends at 11:00. How long is it?' (45 minutes)
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} starts cooking at 4:15 p.m. and finishes at 5:00 p.m., can they work out how long the cooking took?

nodes.description: Estimate lengths using units of inches, feet, centimetres, and metres
evidence: Estimate the length of a classroom object before measuring it
Use a known reference (e.g. width of a finger ≈ 1 cm) to make reasonable estimates
Check estimates by measuring and evaluate how close they were
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looks at a car parked outside, can they estimate roughly how many metres long it is — and then check whether their guess was reasonable?

nodes.description: Identify common uses of halves, quarters and eighths in relation to events and time, such as half-time in a game, half an hour, a quarter of an hour, and an activity split into eight equal time parts
evidence: Describe half-time in a football game as the point when half the playing time is over, and explain that half an hour is 30 minutes because an hour is split into 2 equal parts
Show a quarter of an hour on a clock face as a quarter of the way round
Represent a 16-minute class activity as a strip of eight equal 2-minute parts, colour one part and say it is one eighth of the activity (2 minutes)
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If a 16-minute game is split into 8 equal turns, can {{name}} work out that each turn is one eighth of the game — 2 minutes — and do they know that half an hour is 30 minutes?

nodes.description: Add and subtract amounts of money to give change, using both £ and p in practical contexts
evidence: Calculate the total cost of two or three items priced in pounds and pence
Work out the change from £5 or £10
Record money calculations using £ and p notation correctly (e.g. £3.47)
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} buys a book for £3.50 and a pencil for £1.25 with a £5 note, can they work out exactly how much change they should receive?

nodes.displayName: 测量长度 · 选择工具测量
nodes.description: Measure the length of an object by selecting and using appropriate tools such as rulers, yardsticks, metre sticks, and measuring tapes
evidence: Choose the most appropriate tool for measuring a given object
Align the zero mark of a ruler with the end of the object and read the measurement
Measure lengths in inches, feet, centimetres, and metres using the correct tool
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} needs to measure a piece of fabric about 80 cm long, can they pick the right tool — a short ruler or a tape measure — and use it accurately?

nodes.description: Measure the perimeter of simple 2-D shapes
evidence: Measure each side of a rectangle and add the lengths to find the perimeter
Calculate the perimeter of a regular shape given the side length
Explain that perimeter is the total distance around a shape
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wants to put a decorative border around a rectangular picture frame 20 cm wide and 30 cm tall, can they work out the total length of border needed?

nodes.description: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths to the nearest whole unit and display the data on a line plot
evidence: Measure the lengths of several objects and record the data
Create a line plot with a horizontal scale marked in whole-number units
Interpret a line plot to answer questions about the data
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} measures the length of ten leaves to the nearest cm and records the results, can they display the data on a simple number-line plot — grouping leaves of the same length?

nodes.description: Measure the length of an object using two different length units and describe how the measurements relate to the size of the unit chosen
evidence: Measure a desk in both centimetres and inches and compare the two numbers
Explain that measuring with a smaller unit gives a larger number
Predict whether a measurement in centimetres will be greater or less than in inches
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} measures the same book in centimetres and then in inches, can they explain why the numbers are different even though the book hasn't changed size?

nodes.description: Solve practical money transactions with Australian money involving addition, subtraction and equal groups — totals, change and costs of several identical items — and explain the answer in terms of the purchase
evidence: Work out the total cost of a $4 drink and a $7 sandwich and the change from a $20 note
Find the cost of 3 apples at 50c each by repeated addition
Make 85c using the fewest Australian coins and explain the choice
nodes.assessmentPrompt: At the canteen, if {{name}} buys a $4 drink and a $7 sandwich with a $20 note, can they work out how much change they should get?

nodes.description: Solve word problems involving dollar bills, quarters, dimes, nickels, and pennies, using $ and ¢ symbols appropriately
evidence: Determine the total value of a collection of coins
Solve a word problem about making change with US currency
Use $ and ¢ symbols correctly in answers
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} has 2 quarters, 1 dime, and 3 pennies, can they work out the total — and tell you whether that's enough to buy something costing 65 cents?

nodes.description: Recognise, read and show quarter past and quarter to the hour on an analog clock, linking each to a quarter turn of the minute hand
evidence: Read a clock showing 3:15 as 'quarter past three'
Set the hands of a clock to quarter to seven
Explain that the minute hand has turned a quarter of the way round at quarter past
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looks at an analog clock and the big hand points to the 3, can they say it's 'quarter past'? And can they recognise 'quarter to' when it points to the 9?

nodes.description: Tell and write the time from analogue clocks with Roman-numeral faces (I to XII, including IV, which some clocks show as IIII, and IX), knowing that the minute positions are the same as on a clock with ordinary numbers; and read and write times on 12-hour and 24-hour clocks, knowing that the 24-hour clock runs from 00:00 at midnight to 23:59. Times from 1:00 a.m. to 11:59 a.m. keep the same hour (7:05 a.m. = 07:05); times from 1:00 p.m. to 11:59 p.m. are 12 hours more (3:20 p.m. = 15:20). The 12 o'clock hour is the exception to both: 12:20 p.m., just after noon, stays 12:20, and 12:20 a.m., just after midnight, becomes 00:20. Fluent conversion between 12- and 24-hour times is developed in Year 4
evidence: Read a Roman-numeral clock with the minute hand on IX and the hour hand between IV and V as quarter to five (4:45)
Match the Roman numerals I to XII to the hour positions on a blank clock face, including IV (or IIII), IX and XII
Write 3:20 p.m. as 15:20 and 7:05 a.m. as 07:05, then write 12:20 p.m. as 12:20 and 12:20 a.m. as 00:20, explaining why adding 12 works only for p.m. times from 1 p.m. onwards
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a clock with Roman numerals where the minute hand points to IX and the hour hand is between IV and V, can they read it as quarter to five — and say what time 15:20 on a 24-hour clock means?

nodes.sourceTitle: 用更小的单位提高精度

Choose teaspoons instead of cups to measure how much a small glass holds and explain why
Explain why '3 and a bit hand spans' is less accurate than measuring the same table in counting cubes
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} measures a book with pencils and gets 'about 2', can they see that using smaller paperclips would give a more exact measurement — and a bigger number?

nodes.description: Tell, write and estimate the time to the nearest minute on analogue and digital clocks, using vocabulary such as o'clock, a.m./p.m., morning, afternoon, noon and midnight; record and compare times and durations in seconds, minutes and hours
evidence: Read 7:43 from an analogue clock face and write it on a digital display
Estimate whether brushing teeth takes about 2 seconds, 2 minutes or 2 hours, then time it to check
Compare 1 minute 20 seconds with 75 seconds and say which is longer
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If the kitchen clock shows 7:43, can {{name}} read the exact time and write it as it would look on a digital clock — and say which is longer, 1 minute 20 seconds or 75 seconds?

nodes.description: Know the number of seconds in a minute and the number of days in each month, year, and leap year
evidence: State that there are 60 seconds in a minute
Name the months and state the number of days in each
Explain that a leap year has 366 days and occurs every 4 years
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If you ask {{name}} how many days are in September and whether this year is a leap year, can they answer both — and tell you how many seconds are in a minute?

nodes.description: Read a calendar to identify today's date and the day of the week for a given date, and determine the number of days between two events
evidence: Find 15 March on a calendar page and say which day of the week it is
Write today's date from the classroom calendar in day-month form
Count how many days from 3 June to a birthday on 17 June
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looks at the family calendar, can they find today's date and count how many days are left until their birthday or the school holidays?

nodes.description: Read, write, and convert time between analogue and digital 12-hour and 24-hour clocks
evidence: Convert 3:45 pm to 15:45 in 24-hour time
Read 19:30 and state the 12-hour equivalent as 7:30 pm
Match a set of 12-hour and 24-hour times
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If a train timetable shows a departure at 14:35, can {{name}} convert that to 12-hour clock time — and tell you whether that's morning or afternoon?

nodes.description: Measure areas by counting unit squares (square cm, square m, square in, square ft)

Measure the area of a book cover using square-centimetre tiles
Compare areas of two shapes by counting their unit squares
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} draws a shape on squared centimetre paper, can they find its area by counting the squares — including making a sensible estimate for any partial squares?

nodes.description: Use tiling to demonstrate the distributive property: the area of a rectangle with sides a and (b+c) equals a×b + a×c; use area models to represent the distributive property
evidence: Tile a 3×(4+2) rectangle and show it decomposes into 3×4 and 3×2
Use an area model to compute 6×13 as 6×10 + 6×3
Draw an area model showing 5×(7+3) = 5×7 + 5×3
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wants to work out 6 × 13 by splitting it into 6 × 10 and 6 × 3, can they draw a rectangle divided into two parts to show why that method works?

nodes.description: Find the area of a rectangle by tiling it with unit squares and show that the result equals the product of the side lengths

Explain why the number of rows times the number in each row gives the area
Draw a rectangle on squared paper, tile it, and write the multiplication
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If a rectangular room is 4 m long and 3 m wide, can {{name}} work out its area by tiling it with 1-metre squares in their head — and explain why that equals 4 × 3?

nodes.description: Recognise area as additive; find areas of rectilinear figures by decomposing into non-overlapping rectangles and summing their areas

Find the area of a floor plan shaped like a T by splitting into rectangles
Solve: A room is L-shaped (3m×5m plus 2m×4m) — what is the total area?
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is given an L-shaped room on squared paper, can they split it into two rectangles, find the area of each part, and add them to get the total area?

nodes.description: Multiply side lengths to find areas of rectangles and represent whole-number products as rectangular areas
evidence: Calculate the area of a 7 cm × 9 cm rectangle as 63 cm²
Draw a rectangle with area 36 square units and label its side lengths
Solve: A garden is 8 m by 5 m — what is its area?
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} needs to carpet a room that is 5 m by 4 m, can they work out how much carpet to buy — using multiplication rather than counting squares?

nodes.displayName: 测量单位换算 · 长度与时间单位
nodes.description: Convert between different units of measure (e.g. kilometre to metre, hour to minute, minute to second, year to month, week to day)
evidence: Convert 3 km to 3000 m
State 2 hours = 120 minutes
Convert 5 weeks to 35 days
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is told a journey is 3.5 km, can they convert that to metres — and also turn 2 hours 15 minutes into just minutes?

nodes.description: Recognise the relationship between dollars and cents (100 cents = 1 dollar), read and write amounts in $ and c notation (e.g. $3.45 and 345c), represent the same amount with different combinations of Australian coins and notes, and calculate change in dollars and cents

Show $3.60 in two different ways using Australian coins and notes
Work out the change from a $10 note for a purchase costing $6.40
nodes.assessmentPrompt: At the shops, can {{name}} read a price like $3.45, explain that it means 3 dollars and 45 cents, and work out the change from a $10 note?

nodes.description: Solve word problems involving elapsed time by adding and subtracting time intervals in minutes, including using a number line

Calculate how many minutes between 9:20 and 10:05
Use a number line to show the elapsed time between two events
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} starts football practice at 3:20 p.m. and it lasts 75 minutes, can they work out what time it finishes — using a number line to help?

nodes.description: Estimate, compare, and calculate different measures including money in pounds and pence
evidence: Estimate the length of the classroom in metres
Compare 1.5 kg and 1200 g and identify which is heavier
Calculate the total cost of 3 items at £2.45, £1.30, and £0.75
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is comparing three items costing £2.85, £3.10, and £2.50, can they put them in order from cheapest to most expensive — and work out the total cost?

nodes.displayName: 用半英寸和四分之一英寸记录长度

evidence: Measure five objects to the nearest 1/4 inch
Create a line plot showing the lengths of classmates' pencils in half-inches
Read a line plot and answer questions about the data
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} measures ten pencil lengths to the nearest quarter inch, can they record the data and plot it on a number line split into quarters — then spot which length appears most?

nodes.description: Measure and estimate liquid volumes and masses of objects using grams, kilograms, and litres; solve one-step word problems involving mass or volume
evidence: Estimate the mass of a textbook in grams or kilograms
Read a scale to measure liquid volume in litres
Solve: 3 bags weigh 250 g each — what is the total mass?
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is filling bottles that each hold 250 ml from a 2-litre container of juice, can they work out how many bottles they can fill?

nodes.description: Solve problems involving perimeters of polygons: find perimeter from side lengths, find an unknown side length, and explore rectangles with same perimeter but different areas (or vice versa)

Find the missing side of a pentagon with perimeter 30 cm and four known sides
Draw two rectangles both with perimeter 24 cm but different areas
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If a rectangle has a perimeter of 24 cm and one side is 8 cm, can {{name}} work out the length of the other side — without drawing it?

nodes.description: Understand that a unit square has one square unit of area and that the area of a plane figure is the number of unit squares that cover it without gaps or overlaps
evidence: Identify a unit square and state its area is 1 square unit
Explain why a figure covered by 12 unit squares has area 12 square units
Distinguish between area and perimeter as different measurements
nodes.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} counts the small squares inside a rectangle drawn on squared paper, can they tell you the area — and explain what "one square unit" means?

nodes.description: Apply the area formula (l × w) and perimeter formula (2l + 2w) for rectangles including squares in real-world and mathematical problems; calculate and compare areas using standard units (cm², m²) and estimate areas of irregular shapes
evidence: Find the width of a room given area = 48 m² and length = 8 m
Calculate the area of a square with side 7.5 cm
